Recipe: Easy Guacamole
Yield: 16
Prep 10 min · Total 40 min
Ingredients:
- 2 ripe avocados, peeled and pitted
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 1 ripe tomato, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 lime, juiced
- salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Gather all ingredients.
2. Mash avocado in a medium serving bowl.
3. Stir in onion, tomato, and garlic.
4. Season with lime juice and salt and pepper to taste.
5. Cover and chill guacamole for 30 minutes to allow flavors to blend.

The Best Guacamole Recipe
lines: Recipe: How to Make the Best Guacamole
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lime or lemon juice
- 2-4 tablespoons minced red onion or thinly sliced green onion
- 1-2 serrano (or jalapeño) chiles, stems and seeds removed, minced
- 2 tablespoons cilantro (leaves and tender stems), finely chopped
- Red radish or jicama slices for garnish (optional)
1. Cut the avocados in half. Remove the pit. Score the inside of the avocado with a blunt knife and scoop out the flesh with a spoon. (See How to Cut and Peel an Avocado .) Place in a bowl.
2. Using a fork, roughly mash the avocado. Don’t overdo it! The guacamole should be a little chunky.

3. Sprinkle with salt and lime (or lemon) juice. The acid in the lime juice will provide some balance to the richness of the avocado and will help delay the avocados from turning brown. Add the chopped onion, cilantro, black pepper, and chilis. Chili peppers vary individually in their spiciness. So, start with a half of one chili pepper and add more to the guacamole to your desired degree of heat. Remember that much of this is done to taste because of the variability in the fresh ingredients. Start with this recipe and adjust to your taste.

4. If making a few hours ahead, place plastic wrap on the surface of the guacamole and press down to cover it to prevent air reaching it. (The oxygen in the air causes oxidation which will turn the guacamole brown.) Garnish with slices of red radish or jicama strips. Serve with your choice of store-bought tortilla chips or make your own homemade tortilla chips . Refrigerate leftover guacamole up to 3 days. Note: Chilling tomatoes dulls their flavor. So, if you want to add chopped tomato to your guacamole, add just before serving.

candidates.text:
Recipe: Best Guacamole Recipe
Yield: 6
Prep 15 min · Total 15 min
Ingredients:
- 3 large avocados (ripe)
- 1 Roma tomato (seeded and diced, optional)
- 1/2 medium white onion (diced)
- 1/2 cup cilantro ((1/3 bunch) finely chopped)
- 3 Tbsp lime juice*
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper (freshly ground)
Steps:
1. Cut 3 avocados in half lengthwise, remove pits, scrape the flesh of the avocado out with a spoon. Place in a medium bowl with a flat bottom and mash avocados with a potato masher or a fork to a chunky consistency.
2. Squeeze 3 Tbsp of fresh lime juice directly over avocados while prepping the rest of your ingredients.
3. Add diced tomatoes, onion, and chopped cilantro. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Stir just until combined and serve.

a.title: The Best Guacamole Recipe
lines: Recipe: How to Make the Best Guacamole
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lime or lemon juice
- 2-4 tablespoons minced red onion or thinly sliced green onion
- 1-2 serrano (or jalapeño) chiles, stems and seeds removed, minced
- 2 tablespoons cilantro (leaves and tender stems), finely chopped
- Red radish or jicama slices for garnish (optional)
1. Cut the avocados in half. Remove the pit. Score the inside of the avocado with a blunt knife and scoop out the flesh with a spoon. (See How to Cut and Peel an Avocado .) Place in a bowl.
2. Using a fork, roughly mash the avocado. Don’t overdo it! The guacamole should be a little chunky.

3. Sprinkle with salt and lime (or lemon) juice. The acid in the lime juice will provide some balance to the richness of the avocado and will help delay the avocados from turning brown. Add the chopped onion, cilantro, black pepper, and chilis. Chili peppers vary individually in their spiciness. So, start with a half of one chili pepper and add more to the guacamole to your desired degree of heat. Remember that much of this is done to taste because of the variability in the fresh ingredients. Start with this recipe and adjust to your taste.

4. If making a few hours ahead, place plastic wrap on the surface of the guacamole and press down to cover it to prevent air reaching it. (The oxygen in the air causes oxidation which will turn the guacamole brown.) Garnish with slices of red radish or jicama strips. Serve with your choice of store-bought tortilla chips or make your own homemade tortilla chips . Refrigerate leftover guacamole up to 3 days. Note: Chilling tomatoes dulls their flavor. So, if you want to add chopped tomato to your guacamole, add just before serving.

Recipe: Best Guacamole Recipe
Yield: 6
Prep 15 min · Total 15 min
Ingredients:
- 3 large avocados (ripe)
- 1 Roma tomato (seeded and diced, optional)
- 1/2 medium white onion (diced)
- 1/2 cup cilantro ((1/3 bunch) finely chopped)
- 3 Tbsp lime juice*
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper (freshly ground)
Steps:
1. Cut 3 avocados in half lengthwise, remove pits, scrape the flesh of the avocado out with a spoon. Place in a medium bowl with a flat bottom and mash avocados with a potato masher or a fork to a chunky consistency.
2. Squeeze 3 Tbsp of fresh lime juice directly over avocados while prepping the rest of your ingredients.
3. Add diced tomatoes, onion, and chopped cilantro. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Stir just until combined and serve.
